full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is quickly approaching, and an important step to winning [Super Bowl 61](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/super-bowl-61-odds-post-nfl-draft) could be locking up at least one home playoff game by winning a division title. Just ask the __Seattle Seahawks__, who bested the __Los Angeles Rams__ for the NFC West title before using homefield advantage to beat the Rams for the NFC championship on their way to a Lombardi Trophy.

The 2026 NFL Division Odds show the __Buffalo Bills__ as the most likely team to win their division at -130 odds, and the __Baltimore Ravens__ are the only other odds-on favorite at -115 despite both teams falling short of titles last season. The __Houston Texans__ (+140) and __Kansas City Chiefs__ (+180) round out the AFC’s division favorites. The __Philadelphia Eagles__ (+140) and __Los Angeles Rams__ (+150) have the best odds to win their divisions in the NFC, followed by the __Detroit Lions__ (+180) and __Tampa Bay Buccaneers__ (+185)

Massive underdogs ruled the day as division winners last season. The __Chicago Bears__ (+625), __New England Patriots__ (+550), __Pittsburgh Steelers__ (+550), and __Seattle Seahawks__ (+525) each won their divisions at longer than 5/1 odds. The __Carolina Panthers__ (+425), __Denver Broncos__ (+310), and __Jacksonville Jaguars__ (+310) also claimed titles at longer than 3/1 odds. The __Philadelphia Eagles__ (-150) were the only preseason favorites to win their division. Let’s go division by division to check out the 2026 NFL Division Odds for all 32 teams.

2026 NFL DIVISION ODDS
----------------------

\> Target the Longest Odds to win the division to maximize your potential return. I used DraftKings (DK), FanDuel (FD), BetMGM (MGM), Caesars (CZR), theSCORE Bet (Score), and Bet365 (365) to find the best Division Winner odds as of May 11.

### __AFC EAST__

 Team Longest Odds Shortest Odds Buffalo Bills -130 (multiple) -155 (MGM) New England Patriots +150 (MGM/CZR) +130 (multiple) New York Jets +2000 (FD/MGM) +1800 (multiple) Miami Dolphins +3500 (DK/MGM) +3000 (multiple) 

Sportsbooks have pegged the AFC East as the least competitive division, with two teams listed at +150 odds or shorter and two teams at +2000 odds or longer. The __Buffalo Bills__ own a 56.5% implied odds (-130) to win the AFC East after their six-year title streak came to an end last season. The __New England Patriots__ climbed to the division summit for the first time since 2019, and they’re the only challengers to the Bills at +150 odds (40%). The __New York Jets__ are +2000 (4.8%) to win the AFC East, which they haven’t done since the NFL switched to eight divisions in 2002. The __Miami Dolphins__ face the longest odds to win a division title in the AFC at +3500 (2.8%), so it’s unlikely that they end their 17-year drought without a division title.

#### __Lean__: Buffalo Bills (-130, DraftKings)

Buffalo had an eventful offseason, but not quite as eventful as the one the Patriots had. Mike Vrabel’s off-the-field shenanigans with former national reporter Dianna Russini are still hanging over Buffalo’s only real competition for the division title (sorry, Jets and Dolphins). Buffalo’s owner, Terry Pegula, went on tilt and fired Sean McDermott after the Bills fell short of the AFC Championship game, and he promoted the man responsible for Buffalo’s shortcomings, Brandon Beane, to President of Football Operations. Pegula also promoted 36-year-old Joe Brady to be the next leader of the perennial Super Bowl contenders despite no previous head coaching experience. Drake Maye and the Patriots dethroned the Bills as AFC East champs for the first time since 2019, but Josh Allen gets the Bills back atop the division for the sixth time in seven years. *__If you’re looking to bet the Bills, I would wait to see if A.J. Brown is traded in early June to see if you can get better odds on Buffalo.__*

### __AFC NORTH__

 Team Longest Odds Shortest Odds Baltimore Ravens -115 (DK/CZR) -130 (FD) Cincinnati Bengals +210 (DK/FD) +190 (CZR) Pittsburgh Steelers +600 (FD/Score) +500 (DK) Cleveland Browns +1800 (multiple) +1600 (DK) 

The __Baltimore Ravens__ were a 44-yard field goal away from winning the AFC North for a third straight year, but Tyler Loop’s kick sailed wide right on the final play of the NFL regular season. Baltimore is back to being -115 favorites (53.5% implied odds) in its first season with Jesse Minter in charge after 18 years with John Harbaugh in charge. The __Cincinnati Bengals__ have failed to top 9 wins in three straight seasons, and are +210 (32.3%) to get back to the top of the AFC North for the first time since 2021-22. The __Pittsburgh Steelers__ have just 14.3% implied odds (+600) of winning back-to-back titles as they enter the post-Mike Tomlin era under Mike McCarthy. The __Cleveland Browns__ are the only franchise that’s yet to win a division title since the NFL moved to eight divisions in 2002. They’re facing the NFL’s fourth-longest odds, +1800 (5.3%), to break their drought.

#### __Lean__: Pittsburgh Steelers (+600, FanDuel)

Pittsburgh stunningly won the AFC North, knocking off the rival Ravens on a last-second missed field goal in the final game of the NFL regular season. It was Mike Tomlin’s last signature victory with the franchise. Mike McCarthy took over after Tomlin’s 19-year run without a losing season, and he had a three-year stint with a 12-5 record in Dallas from 2021-23. McCarthy inherited a Steelers roster that’s arguably stronger than the 2025 version if his Green Bay pupil, Aaron Rodgers, can maintain his play at 43 years old. Baltimore is the deserving favorite, and Cincinnati is due to get back in contention with better injury luck, but pesky Pittsburgh is the best value on the board at 6/1 odds.

### __AFC SOUTH__

 Team Longest Odds Shortest Odds Houston Texans +140 (Score) +120 (MGM) Jacksonville Jaguars +210 (DK/MGM) +190 (FD) Indianapolis Colts +400 (MGM) +350 (FD) Tennessee Titans +950 (FD) +700 (Score) 

The AFC South is shaping up to be as competitive as it's been since 2019, which was the only time in the last 15 seasons that all four teams reached a .375 winning percentage or better. The __Houston Texans__ are +140 favorites (41.7% implied odds) to return to the top of the AFC South for the third time in four years with C.J. Stroud and Will Anderson. The __Jacksonville Jaguars__ won their second AFC South title last season since the division formed in 2002, and they own +210 odds (32.3%) to go back-to-back as the champs. The __Indianapolis Colts__ want to end an 11-year drought without a division title — they’ve reached 8+ wins eight times in that span — and they’re +400 (20%) to do it.

#### __Lean__: Tennessee Titans (+950, FanDuel)

I liked the Titans to clear [6.5 wins at plus-odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-win-totals) earlier this offseason, and it shouldn’t be a big surprise that I like Tennessee as a dart throw at their long odds in what should be a competitive AFC South. The organization did its best to bring back the toughness from the Mike Vrabel Era by hiring Robert Saleh, who was prematurely fired by the Jets just five games into the 2024 season. Saleh’s defenses ranked in the top four in YPG allowed in his final three seasons with the Jets, and he got the most out of an injury-ravaged defense in San Francisco last season. Cam Ward showed progress over his final five games after a rocky start to his rookie campaign, and the Titans gave him massive upgrades at receiver in Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson. Tennessee likely needs this division to be jumbled around .500 to win the division, which could happen because I don’t see a dominant team in this group.

### __AFC WEST__

 Team Longest Odds Shortest Odds Kansas City Chiefs +180 (CZR) +160 (DK) Los Angeles Chargers +190 (DK) +180 (CZR) Denver Broncos +225 (DK) +200 (MGM/Score) Las Vegas Raiders +2200 (MGM) +1800 (multiple) 

The AFC West features the most competitive three-way race at the top of a division in the conference. The __Kansas City Chiefs__ are the favorites to win the division at +180 odds (35.7% implied odds) after their nine-year AFC West title streak came to an end last season. They finished two division titles short of matching New England’s streak of 11 consecutive division titles from 2009-19. The __Los Angeles Chargers__ have 34.5% implied odds (+190) of winning their first division crown since 2009 with Philip Rivers and Norv Turner. The __Denver Broncos__ ended Kansas City’s reign at the top of the division, and they’ll look to repeat at 30.8% implied odds (+225). The Chiefs and Broncos have won the last 16 AFC West titles. The __Las Vegas Raiders__ haven’t won a division title since the NFL switched to eight divisions in 2002, and their AFC West title drought is expected to extend to a 24th year at +2200 odds (4.4%).

#### __Lean__: Denver Broncos (+225, DraftKings)

Denver made a splashy move to acquire Jaylen Waddle from the Dolphins, but it’s been an otherwise quiet offseason for a Broncos squad that ended Kansas City’s nine-year run as the NFC West champions. They find themselves behind a Chiefs squad that is at its weakest point in the Patrick Mahomes era, with the quarterback recovering from his season-ending knee injury. The Chargers are also getting plenty of love after switching from Greg Roman to Mike McDaniel at playcaller, so the AFC’s top seed from last season is flying a little under the radar. The Broncos are in a rare position to face a relatively easy schedule as a defending division champion because of all the unexpected division winners from 2025. They get unique games against the Panthers, Steelers, and Jaguars, which could end up being the difference in a division that could be decided by a thin margin. They also open the season against the Chiefs, which is when you want to face Kansas City. Justin Fields will be at quarterback, or Mahomes will be seeing his first action since his knee surgery.

### __NFC EAST__

 Team Longest Odds Shortest Odds Philadelphia Eagles +140 (FD/CZR) +115 (DK) Dallas Cowboys +225 (DK/Score) +190 (CZR) Washington Commanders +525 (MGM) +400 (FD) New York Giants +600 (multiple) +550 (multiple) 

The NFC East had its first repeat division champion since the Eagles won four straight crowns in 2001-04. The __Philadelphia Eagles__ have reached 11+ victories in four consecutive seasons, and are +140 favorites (41.7% implied odds) to win their third consecutive title. The __Dallas Cowboys__ alternated titles with the Eagles since 2021 until last season, and they have 30.8% implied odds (+225) to unseat Philly at the top of the division. The __Washington Commanders__ are coming off a massively disappointing season after reaching the NFC Championship Game in Jayden Daniels first season, and they have +525 odds (16%) to win their first NFC East title since 2020. The __New York Giants__ are longer shots to snap a 14-year division title drought at +600 odds (14.3%).

#### __Lean__: Dallas Cowboys (+225, DraftKings)

The gap between the Eagles and the rest of the NFC East has shrunk this offseason, and it will get a little tighter once Philly trades its #1 receiver. Dallas shored up its defense in free agency, and the draft after ranking last in PPG allowed (30.1) and 30th in YPG allowed (377.0). The Cowboys typically would have an easier schedule than the Eagles because of their second-place schedule, but Philly has a less-demanding slate because of all of the unexpected division winners last season, which is ultimately keeping me off this wager. Dallas has unique games against the Bucs, Packers, and Ravens compared to Philly’s unique games against the Panthers, Bears, and Steelers. *__If you do want to bet on the Cowboys in the NFC East, I would do it before June 1, before their odds shrink a bit after the Eagles trade A.J. Brown.__*

### __NFC NORTH__

 Team Longest Odds Shortest Odds Detroit Lions +185 (DK) +145 (FD) Green Bay Packers +230 (FD/CZR) +185 (Score) Chicago Bears +340 (CZR) +320 (multiple) Minnesota Vikings +600 (multiple) +490 (CZR) 

The NFC North was the only division with all four teams reaching 9+ victories last season, and it projects to be highly competitive once again. The __Detroit Lions__’ two-year run at the top of the division came to an end, but they’re +180 favorites (35.7% implied odds) to get back to the mountaintop. The __Green Bay Packers__ have won 12-of-24 NFC North titles since the NFL went to eight divisions, and they own +230 odds (30.3%) to win their first title since 2021. The __Chicago Bears__ were the longest shots to win a division title last season, which was their second division crown in the last 15 years. There isn’t a lot of faith they can win consecutive NFC North crowns at 22.7% implied odds (+340). The __Minnesota Vikings__ have reached 7+ in 12 straight seasons, and they’re looking to win their fourth division title at +600 (14.3%) in that span.

{{PAYWALL}}

#### __Best Bet__: Detroit Lions (+185, DraftKings)

The Lions failed to extend their division title streak to 3 last season, but they reached 9+ victories for the fourth straight season under Dan Campbell and Jared Goff. The Lions had a relatively quiet offseason, but they should find themselves right back in the mix if they have better injury luck. The Lions lost the [second-most games to injuries](https://ftnfantasy.com/nfl/adjusted-games-lost-2025-no-team-suffered-like-the-cardinals), behind only the Cardinals. And they had particularly bad luck on the defensive side of the ball, where they lost the most games to injuries for the second straight season. Detroit slid to third in the NFC North last season, but it will benefit greatly this year against the [NFL’s easiest schedule](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/analysis/nfl-strength-of-schedule/). The Lions face unique games against the Giants, Cardinals, and Titans, which is a significantly easier slate of extra games compared to the Packers (LAR, Dal, Hou), Bears (Sea, Phi, Jax), and Vikings (SF, Was, Ind).

### __NFC SOUTH__

 Team Longest Odds Shortest Odds Tampa Bay Buccaneers +185 (FD) +160 (Score) New Orleans Saints +300 (Score/CZR) +265 (DK) Carolina Panthers +375 (Score) +300 (DK/265) Atlanta Falcons +450 (DK) +275 (Score) 

The NFC South is the most wide-open division entering the season, with all four teams listed between +185 and +450 odds to walk away as champions. It’s also been the NFC’s weakest division in recent years, with all four teams finishing with a losing record last season. At least three of the four teams have finished under .500 in five of the last eight years. The NFC’s longest division title streak ended at five straight crowns for the __Tampa Bay Buccaneers__ last season, but they’re back to being the favorites at +185 odds (35.1% implied odds). The __New Orleans Saints__ surged to +300 odds (25%) on the strength of a strong finish to 2025 once Tyler Shough entered the lineup. The __Carolina Panthers__ have 21.1% implied odds (+375) of repeating as division champs after ending their seven-year postseason drought. The __Atlanta Falcons__ face +450 odds (18.2%) to win the division for the first time since 2016 and to end the NFC’s longest playoff drought at eight seasons.

#### __Brolley’s Best Bet__: New Orleans Saints (+300, theScore Bet)

I [bet against](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-win-totals) the Buccaneers winning more than 8.5 games at plus odds earlier this offseason, and I’d prefer to take a chance on the Saints at +300 odds. New Orleans surged late in the season under Tyler Shough, and it could continue in 2026 after they loaded up on weapons to surround him. They made a bigger splash at running back than expected by signing the Louisiana-native Travis Etienne to a long-term deal. The Saints had a top-heavy receiving corps led by Chris Olave, but they changed their situation by selecting Jordan Tyson eighth overall, Oscar Delp in the third round, and Bryce Lance in the fourth round, which gives Tyler Shough a full deck at receiver. The NFC South could be a true toss-up with all four teams tightening up this offseason, but I like the direction of the Saints the most heading into 2026. It doesn’t hurt that New Orleans faces the [second-easiest schedule](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/analysis/nfl-strength-of-schedule/), which could be the difference at the top of the division.

### __NFC WEST__

 Team Longest Odds Shortest Odds Los Angeles Rams +150 (Score) +130 (FD) Seattle Seahawks +175 (FD/CZR) +160 (multiple) San Francisco 49ers +275 (MGM) +240 (CZR) Arizona Cardinals +9000 (DK) +3000 (FD) 

The NFC West featured three teams that combined for 38 victories last season, and it's shaping up to be another competitive race to the top. The __Los Angeles Rams__ are the slight favorites at +150 (40% implied odds), which would be Sean McVay’s fifth division title in 10 seasons. The __Seattle Seahawks__, the defending Super Bowl champions, own +175 odds (36.4%) to repeat as NFC West champs for the first time since 2013-14. The __San Francisco 49ers__ have reached 12+ victories in three of their last four seasons, and have 26.7% implied odds (+275) of winning the division. The __Arizona Cardinals__ basically have no chance of winning the NFC West, as oddsmakers have pegged them with the NFL’s longest odds to win a division at a whopping +9000 (1.1%).

#### __Lean__: Seattle Seahawks (+175, FanDuel)

I have the Rams [ranked](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) as the NFL’s best team, slightly ahead of the defending Super Bowl champions, but I don’t have a whole lot of daylight between the two teams. I’m slightly worried about the Seahawks experiencing a Super Bowl hangover, but not enough to take the longer odds with the team that faces the easier schedule. Seattle owns unique games against the Bears, Patriots, and Panthers compared to the Packers, Bills, and Buccaneers for Los Angeles. I’m staying away from the bet because the 49ers have the easiest schedule in the division overall once again, and they could easily climb to the top of the division if they ever had better injury luck.

### Brolley’s NFL Division Best Bets

+ NFC North Winner: __Detroit Lions__ (+185, DraftKings). *Risk 1 unit to win 1.85 units. Placed at 1:31 p.m. on May 13.*

+ NFC South Winner: __New Orleans Saints__ (+300, theScore Bet). *Risk .5 units to win 1.5 units. Placed at 1:32 p.m. on May 13.*
